doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Photo session: wagons, parades and goodbyes
title: Alfred Laine as second cornet and his stroke
summary: Laine praises his son Alfred as his best second cornet, recalls two bands in a Mardi Gras parade, and his illness and death.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: The best second cornet player I ever had in my band was Alfred Lane. Oh, yeah. Hmm.
Well, I think we better...
When were we speaking about that?
Huh?
When were we speaking about Alfred Lane being second cornet player?
I believe yesterday or this morning. I don't know.

Yesterday. Since lately we were speaking about it. Sitting out on Aunt Gary. You couldn't take it away from him. I see they're proud of him. Yeah. We played in the Mardi Gras parade. We had two bands together. See?
Poor fellow when he got that stroke.
One band, a headache, he had a meal and a band with me.
Didn't want him to blow. Every other tree, two floats and two bands.
In the back of his head.
In the back of his head. All the music. He played in the music. He played in the music. He played in the music.
He used to get bands out of the city.
That wasn't enough. All around. In December he was...
He swallowed all up.
New York. He's come from New York down here. Yeah.
So...
They claim was from the insulin. We played...
The Sackwins. He got that. I got the marts that was.
I mean... He didn't last... Let's see. And that boy I'm on... January or February...
He died to push the marts. Boy, you took care of that melody. So sweet.
I was proud.
And then...
Can't get you here.

The guy ahead of me... I can't think of his name anymore. He jumped from my band into his band to learn him how to play second. Leader of their band. The other band. Yeah. Alfred Lane. I spoke to her. I told her about that. It was yesterday. It wasn't this morning. It was yesterday. Yesterday. Speaking about it.
Yesterday, yeah.
We're talking about music and stuff like that. And production and wanting that too. That boy sure could play a swell horn. Beautiful.
